Terminal AI agent KTPH001 toolsKTPH000

korTTY's Terminal AI Agent is a controlled automation workflow that enables safe, intelligent command execution on remote servers — and, since the execution engine was decoupled behind an KTPH000 abstraction (SSH exec-channel and local-process backends), in KTPH001local shellsKTPH002 on Windows, macOS and Linux too. Unlike naive automation, the agent probes the session state, reasons about each step, and waits for human approval before executing system-changing commands.
SSH vs. local shells

In local shells, commands use a native local backend (PowerShell via KTPH000, KTPH001, or POSIX KTPH002) and the environment probe and system prompt are platform-aware. The agent captures the interactive shell's current directory when a run starts and uses that same snapshot for its probe and every command in the run. Local-shell limitations: no KTPH003/administrator elevation on Windows. The JobScheduler's headless AI-agent action stays SSH-only.
KTPH000
RAG is explicit for autonomous work

Knowledge stores assigned to normal Text/Coding requests do not automatically expand the Terminal AI Agent, Planning, Swarm, or scheduled job context. Those autonomous flows require an explicit RAG opt-in; see KTPH000RAG knowledge storesKTPH001. This prevents a background workflow from reading indexed local sources merely because the same model profile is used for interactive chat.
Command variantsKTPH000

The Terminal AI Agent is triggered via shortcut commands at the shell prompt. When enabled in KTPH000Settings KTPH002 AIKTPH001, KorTTY intercepts these commands locally instead of sending them to the server:
The base command name is configurable in KTPH003Settings KTPH005 AIKTPH004. If you rename KTPH000, KorTTY automatically derives the matching KTPH001 and KTPH002 commands. The same settings page can:
Make the command name case-insensitive
Disable the per-run setup dialog (uses the configured default profile when disabled)
Note

KorTTY recognizes these shortcuts in the connector input path before normal shell execution. Keyboard input and clipboard paste are assembled from the same byte stream, so pasted file names and Unicode text are included in the request, the complete prompt is saved in agent history, and one Enter produces exactly one agent run.
Command purposesKTPH000

KTPH001KTPH000KTPH002 — Execute safe terminal commands to accomplish a goal. The agent inspects the session, plans non-interactive commands, requests approval when needed, and (by default) writes the final answer back to the terminal. The run dialog offers a KTPH003Show final answer in the terminal tooKTPH004 option: leave it on to mirror the answer into the terminal, or turn it off so the answer stays only in the AI agent activity panel. Either way the commands still run and their output and any files they create remain on the server; only the display of the final answer text changes. The last choice is remembered as the default.

KTPH001KTPH000KTPH002 — Get a non-executing answer about the current session context without running any commands. When started from the terminal right-click menu (KTPH003AI → Ask AI AgentKTPH004) with text selected, the selection is sent along as context, so the question is answered about the selected output or script.

KTPH002KTPH000 / KTPH001KTPH003 — Enter planning mode first. The agent asks clarifying questions, proposes approaches, generates a final plan, and runs implementation only after you click KTPH004ImplementKTPH005.
ExamplesKTPH000
TAB completion and prompt historyKTPH000
At the shell prompt, TAB completion is enhanced for agent commands:
Type the agent command name (e.g., KTPH000) then press KTPH005KTPH004KTPH006 to show command variants (KTPH001, KTPH002, KTPH003).

Type the command + a space (e.g., KTPH000) then press KTPH002KTPH001KTPH003 to show recent agent-prompt history. Each row displays the prompt and the date/time it was last run, de-duplicated by prompt text (newest first).
Prompts longer than 60 characters are shortened with an ellipsis for readability; the full prompt is still inserted when selected.
The history popup is resizable — drag the grip in the bottom-right corner — and remembers its size across restarts. It shows a vertical scrollbar when the history exceeds the popup height.

In the history popup, click a row's ✕ button (or press KTPH001KTPH000KTPH002 on keyboards with a forward-delete key) to remove a single prompt, or use KTPH003Clear allKTPH004 (two-step confirm) to wipe the entire history. Deletions are saved immediately.
Outside this context, KTPH001KTPH000KTPH002 remains normal shell completion.
History size is configurable in KTPH000Settings KTPH002 AIKTPH001 (default 20, range 5–100).
How the AI Agent worksKTPH000
The Terminal AI Agent follows a strict, safe execution loop:

KTPH000Probe the sessionKTPH001 — KorTTY probes the active terminal session with a non-interactive command and records compact context: current user, host, operating system, active terminal working directory, sudo availability, disk path, and recent command state.
KTPH000Send context to the modelKTPH001 — KorTTY sends the user task, probe snapshot, previous command results, active AI Skills, and optionally web-tool availability to the selected AI profile.
KTPH000Model returns a JSON decisionKTPH001 — The model must return a strict JSON response: run commands, ask for confirmation, finish, or block.
KTPH000Validate the decisionKTPH001 — KorTTY validates the JSON schema and command constraints. Invalid responses are repaired once; unsafe or unsupported decisions are rejected.

KTPH002Execute approved commandsKTPH003 — KorTTY runs approved commands through the active backend: SSH exec channels for SSH sessions, or a fresh local process for local shells. Each command starts in the tracked active terminal directory captured for this run. A KTPH000 inside a one-shot command does not persist to the next command, while an interactive KTPH001 completed before the run is included in the captured directory.

KTPH000Iterate or concludeKTPH001 — Command output is added to the activity panel and to the next model turn until the task completes, is blocked, cancelled, or the turn limit is reached (8 turns maximum).
Suitable tasksKTPH000
Inspecting files, directories, package state, logs, service state, and system configuration
Creating or modifying scripts and configuration files when the task asks for it
Running tests, syntax checks, linters, or read-only diagnostic commands
Summarizing command output and explaining findings
Planning multi-step operational changes before implementation
Not suitable forKTPH000
Interactive full-screen programs such as KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002, KTPH003, KTPH004, or commands that wait for prompts
Long-running daemons or commands without clear completion
Secret exfiltration or blind destructive commands
Web research for local files unless the user explicitly asks for external/current information
Tip

For local file review tasks, name the file in your prompt. The agent should then inspect it with shell commands such as KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002, or language-specific syntax checks. When an internet-enabled profile is active, KorTTY still keeps web tools away from local file planning unless your task clearly asks for current or external information.
Activity panelKTPH000
Terminal-targeted agent runs use an inline activity panel at the bottom of the current terminal split.
Panel featuresKTPH000

KTPH000Run tabsKTPH001 — Multiple concurrent runs appear as closable tabs. Click a tab to select it; only the selected tab's run is controlled by run-control keys and buttons. Up to 5 concurrent runs per split.

KTPH000ControlsKTPH001 — Each run has reload, pause/resume, cancel buttons, and per-row copy/snippet actions. The reload button re-runs the command with the KTPH002currently activeKTPH003 AI profile, so switching profiles between runs takes effect on the rerun.

KTPH000DetailsKTPH001 — The panel shows the user prompt in a two-line scrollable field, agent messages, read/run actions, task timing, reported token usage, semantic activity markers, and collapsible details.
KTPH001AI profile rowKTPH002 — Every run log starts with an KTPH000 entry, so the protocol records which profile and model produced the run.

KTPH002Model reasoningKTPH003 — Expanding a 💭 thinking row shows the model's full reasoning when the provider exposes it (Anthropic extended thinking when the profile's Reasoning effort is enabled, OpenAI-compatible KTPH000, LM Studio reasoning output, or KTPH001 blocks from local CLI models). Models without exposed reasoning keep the short decision summary.

KTPH000Status barKTPH001 — When collapsed, the panel shows a compact status bar with the run prompt, state, pause/cancel buttons, and expand button. A spinner shows while the agent is working; a bold ✋ marker signals when user input is required.
KTPH000Keep collapsedKTPH001 — Use KTPH002Keep collapsedKTPH003 to make the panel start minimized and stay collapsed when new activity or input prompts arrive. You can still expand manually.
KTPH000ResizingKTPH001 — Drag the resize handle to change panel height. Enable KTPH002Remember sizeKTPH003 to persist height and font size across application restarts.
KTPH000Parallel splitsKTPH001 — Different splits can run their own agent tasks in parallel; each split has its own activity panel.
KTPH000Font controlsKTPH001 — Use KTPH002A−KTPH003 and KTPH004A+KTPH005 to change the activity font size.

KTPH000ExportKTPH001 — Save the current run or all panel-history runs as Markdown, plain text, YAML, XML, JSON, PDF, or Asciidoctor. Exports include the AI profile, model/LLM, reasoning status, run timestamps, total runtime, per-activity runtimes, token usage, and detail text.
KTPH000Expand allKTPH001 — Keep activity details open instead of compacting them. This option is saved globally.
Panel placementKTPH000
Use KTPH000View → AI Agent PanelKTPH001 to choose where the activity panel appears:
KTPH000At BottomKTPH001 (default) — The activity panel appears below the terminal split where the run was started.

KTPH000Dock Left / Dock RightKTPH001 — The panel appears as a resizable side panel docked to the main window (like the file browser). In side mode there is one outer tab per terminal of the active tab, with runs stacked vertically. Dragging the divider resizes the dock; placement and width are remembered across restarts. Switching to another terminal tab swaps the dock to that tab's terminals.
Status indicatorsKTPH000
A per-terminal AI-agent status icon appears in the Dashboard and prefixed to the terminal tab title, aggregated across that terminal's runs and refreshed about once a second:
KTPH000✋KTPH001 — Awaiting user input (approval or sudo password)
KTPH000⚡KTPH001 — Working (agent is actively planning or running commands)
KTPH000⏸KTPH001 — Paused (run is parked at a safe checkpoint)
KTPH000✓KTPH001 — Finished (run completed successfully)
Activity iconsKTPH000
Activity rows use semantic emoji icons (static, non-blinking):
Icon
Meaning
Request or input: write/create file
Action: read file/directory
Action: run/execute command
Action: directory operation
Context: package manager
Context: service or system
Action: network operation
Action: inspect/analyze
State: thinking/reasoning
Output: message or result
Required: awaiting user input (sudo/approval)
State: error or failed activity
State: cancelled activity
Red styling is reserved for error and failed states.
Safety and failure handlingKTPH000
KorTTY enforces multiple guardrails around agent execution:
Command limitsKTPH000
KTPH000Per-turn limitKTPH001 — A maximum of 3 commands per turn prevents runaway automation.
KTPH003Non-interactive onlyKTPH004 — The agent rejects interactive commands (like KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002) that would hang in a non-interactive command backend.
KTPH004Mutating-command detectionKTPH005 — Commands that change the system (KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002, KTPH003, etc.) are flagged for confirmation unless the agent has auto-approval bypass.
Privilege handlingKTPH000
KTPH000Sudo detectionKTPH001 — The agent detects whether the current user has sudo access and whether a password is required.
KTPH001Passwordless sudoKTPH002 — When KTPH000 (no-password sudo) is available, the agent uses it without prompting.
KTPH000Password promptsKTPH001 — When a password is required, the agent requests it via an activity-panel password input field (masked, not echoed to the terminal).
KTPH000Password retriesKTPH001 — Up to 3 wrong-password retries are allowed before the run cancels.

KTPH000Mutating commandsKTPH001 — By default, the agent asks for approval before running commands that modify the system (unless auto-approval is enabled in settings).
KTPH000Confirmation dialogKTPH001 — The approval dialog shows the planned commands and their purposes. You can approve once, approve all remaining commands in the run, or cancel.

KTPH000Sudo preflightKTPH001 — After accepting a planning report, if the plan requires sudo and your SSH session requires a sudo password, KorTTY performs the preflight check immediately after acceptance so execution is not interrupted later.
Directory trackingKTPH000

KTPH000Active directoryKTPH001 — Terminal shortcut runs use KorTTY's tracked current directory for both SSH and local shells. For a local run, korTTY refreshes the shell process directory on macOS/Linux, accepts an existing absolute path from a native PowerShell/cmd prompt, then uses the last trusted directory or the connection's start directory only when no directory-changing command made that fallback stale.

KTPH000Stable run snapshotKTPH001 — The directory is captured outside the JavaFX thread when the run begins. The environment probe and all commands in that run use the same snapshot even if the interactive shell changes directory later.

KTPH004Unknown or foreign directoryKTPH005 — After KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002, or KTPH003, an unknown directory is an error rather than a silent fallback. WSL, Git Bash, Cygwin, and custom commands remain best-effort on Windows; if their path namespace cannot be mapped to the local filesystem, korTTY stops the action instead of targeting a same-named file elsewhere.
KTPH000SSH directory lossKTPH001 — If a tracked remote directory no longer exists, korTTY retries the probe from the SSH default directory and reports the issue.

KTPH001Not lockedKTPH002 — While a terminal-targeted run is active, normal typing is still allowed. You can keep typing in the shell prompt and launch new KTPH000 commands (they open new tabs).
KTPH000Run-control keys onlyKTPH001 — Only run-control keys are intercepted:

KTPH002KTPH000KTPH003+KTPH004KTPH001KTPH005 — Toggle the selected run's thinking details

KTPH004Input hardeningKTPH005 — A second collapsible panel that asks the AI to build an input-validation guard block into the generated script: parameter allowlists and length limits, file format checks, a maximum input-file size controlled by the adjustable KTPH000 script variable, security warnings in the script's log, and a KTPH001 / KTPH002 override. The guard checks file metadata before it reads content, and KTPH003 means unlimited. Strictly opt-in — the master check box starts unticked. See KTPH006Input hardeningKTPH007.
